hypothesis: The ATR>30 regime filter discovered in EXP-0005 holds out-of-sample across multiple walk-forward windows, confirming it is a genuine predictive feature rather than an in-sample artifact.

protocol.train_logic: For each fold, test all ATR thresholds in-sample, record best threshold
protocol.test_logic: Apply ATR>30 (fixed) to the out-of-sample test period; compare vs unfiltered baseline
protocol.pass_criterion: ATR>30 beats baseline in >= 3 of 4 test folds

fold_4.failure_note: Only 9 qualifying trades in July — insufficient sample. July avg ATR=19.58 pts (lowest of 6 months); ATR>30 spikes are isolated noise events, not a sustained regime.

threshold_stability.detail: In-sample best threshold varies: ATR>25 (fold 1, Feb-Mar only), ATR>35 (folds 2-4). The selection is unstable. However, ATR>30 outperforms no_filter in 3/4 OOS folds, confirming robustness even when the exact threshold is not optimal.
threshold_stability.practical_implication: ATR>30 is a reasonable conservative threshold. ATR>35 may be better but too trade-restrictive in shorter data windows.

leakage_notes: ATR computed from rolling(10) past bars only. No bar i+1 data used. Training threshold selection uses only training period data. Filter applied before strategy sees bars — no contamination.
conclusion: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED — ATR filter PASSES walk-forward validation (3/4 folds). The edge is not pure in-sample overfitting. Key findings: (1) ATR>30 filter boosts avg OOS monthly return from +49.4% to +88.0%. (2) Filter fails in July because July's sustained ATR (~19.58) means ATR>30 events are sparse spikes (only 9 trades), not a regime. (3) In-sample optimal threshold shifts between ATR>25 and ATR>35 across folds — slight instability in threshold selection. CRITICAL CAVEAT: All data is from a single 6-month window with only one clear high-vol regime (March). Generalizability beyond this regime class requires more data.
